session.question: How does the combined detecion of KAI1 and VEGF improve the diagnosis of HCC?
session.answer:
Combined detection of KAI1 and VEGF improves hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) diagnosis by leveraging two complementary biomarkers with opposite dysregulation patterns: KAI1 is downregulated, whereas VEGF is upregulated in HCC. This dual-marker approach outperforms either marker alone and yields a more reliable diagnostic panel. (zhang2014expressioncharacteristicsof chunk 1)

Specifically, KAI1 alone showed stronger diagnostic performance than VEGF, with an AUC (area under the ROC curve) of 0.907 versus 0.779 for VEGF. Serum KAI1 alone achieved 86.96% sensitivity and 83.06% accuracy. When KAI1 and VEGF were combined, sensitivity increased to 91.86%, accuracy improved to 84.68%, and negative predictive value rose to 78.79%. (zhang2014expressioncharacteristicsof chunk 1)

Thus, the combined assay enhances case detection, reduces false negatives, and provides better overall diagnostic reliability than single-marker testing for HCC. (zhang2014expressioncharacteristicsof chunk 1)

From Wu Zhang, Cheng-Guang Zhao, Hong-Yu Sun, Wei-E Zheng, and Hua Chen. Expression characteristics of kai1 and vascular endothelial growth factor and their diagnostic value for hepatocellular carcinoma. Gut and Liver, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.5009/gnl13331, doi:10.5009/gnl13331.

pqac-ed1b5f37: The excerpt is about alcohol-enhanced progression and metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through ROS, NF-κB activation, and upregulation of VEGF and MCP-1. It reports higher VEGF expression in HCC tissues of alcohol drinkers and links VEGF to tumor angiogenesis, growth, and metastasis. However, the excerpt does not mention KAI1, nor does it discuss any diagnostic performance or combined diagnostic value of KAI1 and VEGF for HCC.
From Fei Wang, Jin-Lian Yang, Ke-ke Yu, Mei Xu, You-zhi Xu, Li Chen, Yan-min Lu, Hao-shu Fang, Xin-yi Wang, Zhong-qian Hu, Fei-fei Li, Lixin Kan, Jia Luo, and Si-Ying Wang. Activation of the nf-κb pathway as a mechanism of alcohol enhanced progression and metastasis of human hepatocellular carcinoma. Molecular Cancer, 2015. URL: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12943-014-0274-0, doi:10.1186/s12943-014-0274-0.

pqac-a5afc759: The excerpt is about a 2014 study identifying a serum microRNA panel for hepatitis B virus–related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), not about KAI1 and VEGF. It reports that a combined miRNA set improved diagnostic accuracy for HCC, with AUCs of 0.887 and 0.879 in training and validation cohorts, and AUCs of 0.893 versus healthy controls and 0.892 versus cirrhosis. However, it contains no information on KAI1, VEGF, their combined detection, sensitivity, specificity, or whether the markers complement each other in HCC diagnosis.
From Youwen Tan, Guohong Ge, Tengli Pan, Danfeng Wen, Li Chen, Xuejun Yu, Xinbei Zhou, and Jianhe Gan. A serum microrna panel as potential biomarkers for hepatocellular carcinoma related with hepatitis b virus. PLoS ONE, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0107986, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0107986.
